mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, increasing present value and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This mechanism is always active and does not require specific threshold conditions.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in a rolling 12-month window.

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate below 4.0% indicates a tight labor market, which typically precedes stronger consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In instances where UNRATE is below 4.0%, the 5-day forward SPX returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand and economic expansion, which is a leading indicator of positive equity market performance over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict positive 60-day SPX returns in more than 40% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation environment (CPIAUCSL > 230), the Federal Reserve is likely to implement tighter monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 230, the 20-day forward SPX returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC for CPIAUCSL as a predictor of negative returns is below -0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates strengthening manufacturing and economic activity, which supports corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This mechanism is always active and does not require specific threshold conditions.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for INDPRO as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between INDPRO and 20-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in a rolling 12-month window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll growth rate exceeding 0.5% signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In instances where PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5%, the 5-day forward SPX returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent expansion in quarterly GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates broad-based economic strength, which is a leading indicator of positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising GDPC1 and HOUST fails to predict positive 20-day SPX returns in more than 40% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising above 2.0%), the S&P 500 tends to underperform as higher interest rates reduce the present value of future cash flows and increase borrowing costs for corporations, leading to negative returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.0%, the 60-day forward SPX returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of negative returns is below -0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.
